consumer: The dialogue/mission condition evaluator (conditional_t<T>::set_has_item lambda) asking the yes/no 'does the avatar actor have item X' via actor->charges_of(item_id) > 0 || actor->has_amount(item_id, 1).
scope: only the character/avatar's own carried possession (on-person: wielded/worn/inventory) as charges_of/has_amount counts it, not nearby reachable items or any map region
decisive_source: src/condition.cpp::conditional_t<T>::set_has_item builds a lambda that EVALUATES a boolean possession predicate over the alpha/beta character actor using charges_of and has_amount; that returned value is what a mission/dialogue check consumes.
divergence: Avatar carries ammo charges nested inside a magazine inside a worn container: the engine predicate charges_of/has_amount accounts for it and returns true, but re-deriving the yes/no from the avatar.carried_items[] snapshot (which enumerates wielded/worn/inventory entries and, per visit_internal, does not descend into gun/magazine contents) yields false — exposing the wrong authority.
